practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and keep a .env.example placeholder rather than committing secrets into the repo.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any DB credentials) from environment variables at runtime and never commit secrets into the repo; provide a .env.example placeholder instead.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance (process-wide singleton) rather than creating a new client per request; initialize it once and reuse across handlers (cache on module/global scope).
practices.prior_belief: Create and reuse a single MongoClient connection (one instance per Node.js process) rather than opening a new connection per request; configure connection pool size (maxPoolSize) and timeouts at startup.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB (connection strings include tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for the connection and validate server certificates; never disable certificate validation in production.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using MongoDB Shell

practices.practice: Handle transient errors with bounded exponential-backoff retries and specifically detect and back off / retry on throttling (429) or transient network errors rather than unlimited retries.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential-backoff retries for transient errors and specifically handle 429 (throttling / rate limit) responses and network timeouts; surface/fail after a bounded number of retries.
practices.how_found: "Azure DocumentDB transient fault handling 429 exponential backoff"

practices.practice: Provision capacity by choosing the appropriate cluster compute tier (M10, M30, etc.) and storage sizing and monitor CPU/IOPS/storage/connection metrics (throughput is driven by compute/storage tier rather than Cosmos-style RU tokens); optimize queries to reduce IO and index usage.
practices.prior_belief: Provision and monitor throughput (RUs) for the database/collections and design queries to minimize RU cost: use projections to fetch only needed fields and avoid returning large documents unnecessarily.

practices.practice: Choose an appropriate shard key (partition key) based on query and write patterns—pick a key that localizes the most-common reads or that evenly distributes writes to avoid hot partitions.
practices.prior_belief: Choose an appropriate partition key for collections (e.g., applicationId or customerId) to avoid hot partitions and cross-partition fan-out; design queries to be targeted to a single partition where possible.

practices.practice: Create indexes on frequently filtered or sorted fields used by the pipeline (e.g., applicationId, status, createdAt, credit_score) so lookups and sorts are covered by indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes on frequently filtered/sorted fields used by the pipeline (e.g., applicationId, status, createdAt, applicant.ssn or normalized email) so lookups and sorts are covered by the index.

practices.practice: Avoid unindexed queries and full-collection scans in production; use explain('executionStats') to verify queries use indexes and to examine keysExamined/docsExamined/execTime metrics.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid unindexed queries and full-collection scans in production; use explain() during development to verify queries use indexes and examine their RU/IO cost.

practices.practice: For vector similarity search use a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch) and choose the implementation (DiskANN / HNSW / IVF) appropriate to scale and recall requirements; create the index with correct dimensions and similarity metric (COS/L2/IP).
practices.prior_belief: For vector similarity search, create a dedicated vector index on the embedding field with parameters tuned to the embedding dimension (e.g., HNSW/IVF parameters appropriate for your vector length); keep embeddings as dense numeric arrays in a single field.

practices.practice: When performing ANN/vector queries, tune candidate sizes and index/query parameters and fetch only required document fields (projections) and apply post-filters to reduce IO, memory use, and latency.
practices.prior_belief: When performing ANN/vector queries, limit candidate sizes and fetch only required document fields (projection) before post-filtering/deduplication to control RU and memory usage.

practices.practice: Make pipeline output idempotent—use upsert (e.g., updateOne with upsert: true) keyed by applicationId or decisionId so retries don't create duplicate documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use idempotent writes for pipeline output (upsert by applicationId or decisionId) so repeated/failed retries do not create duplicates; seed scripts should be idempotent (check and upsert).
practices.source_name: Build a Node.js console app with Azure DocumentDB (perform common operations / upsert example)

practices.practice: Observe the maximum BSON document size (16 MB) and avoid embedding very large blobs—store large binary or long text in external storage (e.g., Azure Blob Storage) and keep references in DocumentDB.
practices.prior_belief: Limit document size to the platform maximum and avoid embedding very large blobs; if storing large text or binary (attachments), use external storage (e.g., Blob Storage) and store references in DocumentDB.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use TTL (time-to-live) indexes for ephemeral or cache-like collections (create an index with expireAfterSeconds) to automatically expire old documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL (time-to-live) indexes for ephemeral or cache-like collections (e.g., temporary embeddings, intermediate pipeline artifacts) to automatically purge old data and save storage/RUs.
practices.source_name: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB (index types / TTL)

practices.practice: Perform input validation and sanitize free-text prior to passing it to an LLM and avoid storing unnecessary PII; for data-at-rest encryption of sensitive fields prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) where compliance requires it.
practices.prior_belief: Perform input validation and sanitize any free-text fields before passing them to the LLM layer or using them in DB queries; avoid storing PII unless necessary and encrypt sensitive fields at rest or in application layer.
practices.how_found: "Azure DocumentDB LLM PII sanitization"; "Azure DocumentDB guidance PII storage and encryption"

practices.practice: Use least-privilege credentials: prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or create DB users with only necessary privileges rather than a full admin key; rotate secrets and prefer Key Vault references for deployment-time secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Use least-privilege credentials for the app — create a DB user with only required privileges (read on applications, write on decisions) rather than using a full admin key; rotate credentials regularly.

practices.practice: Design queries and indexes to avoid cross-partition sorts and aggregations; when heavy aggregation is required, pre-aggregate or target a single partition where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Design queries and indexes to avoid cross-partition sorts and aggregations; where heavy aggregation is required, consider pre-aggregating or using targeted partition queries.

practices.practice: Close the MongoClient cleanly on application shutdown and only close when the process is exiting, ensuring background tasks are drained to avoid leaked connections or partial writes.
practices.prior_belief: Close the MongoClient cleanly on application shutdown and ensure background pipeline tasks are drained before exit to avoid leaked connections or partial writes.

practices.practice: Instrument and monitor cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage), query/slow-query logs, connection pool metrics and throttling (429) via Azure Monitor / Log Analytics and alert on high throttling or resource saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor query latency, RU consumption, throttling (429s), connection pool metrics and errors using Azure Monitor / Application Insights and add alerts for high throttling or errors.

practices.practice: Mock the database and external LLMs in unit tests and keep live-cluster integration tests gated or explicit (unit tests should be hermetic).
practices.prior_belief: Mock the DB and LLM in unit tests (as you did) and reserve live-cluster integration tests for CI or gated tests that explicitly use the DOCUMENTDB_URI; keep unit tests hermetic.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB testing guidance mock mongodb unit tests"; "Azure DocumentDB LLM mocking guidance"

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document transactions and the API exposes startSession()/withTransaction() that can run across multiple logical and physical shards (be aware of transaction timeouts and limits).
practices.prior_belief: Avoid long-running multi-document transactions across different partitions; prefer idempotent single-document updates or orchestrated workflows with compensation logic if multi-collection atomicity is required.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use projections to limit returned fields (exclude large vectors or unneeded subdocuments) and prefer range-based or cursor-based pagination over deep skip-based offsets.
practices.prior_belief: Use projections to limit returned fields (e.g., exclude large embedding vectors when not needed) and paginate results rather than relying on skip for deep offsets; prefer range-based pagination by indexed timestamp or _id.

practices.practice: When storing embeddings, persist retrieval metadata (source document id, chunk id, text snippet, model name, and vector dimension) as separate indexed fields alongside the vector to allow efficient retrieval after a vector match.
practices.prior_belief: When storing embeddings, persist metadata used by agents (source doc id, chunk id, text snippet) as separate indexed fields to allow efficient retrieval after a vector hit.

notes: I inspected the sample app (seed, db, pipeline, agents) and used official Microsoft docs (learn.microsoft.com) via searches plus the installed DocumentDB skills. Many general MongoDB best practices are explicitly present in the DocumentDB public docs and the installed skills (singleton MongoClient, TLS, retry handling, index design, explain(), vector index choices, TTL, 16MB doc size, upsert examples, monitoring/alerts, compute-tier provisioning). A few app-level concerns tied to LLM usage (sanitization of free text before LLM, explicit guidance on storing decision rationales) are not present in Azure DocumentDB documentation and are recorded as prior_knowledge_only entries (K14, K19). K05 (RU-based provisioning) and K20 (avoid cross-partition transactions) were contradicted for Azure DocumentDB: the public record indicates capacity is chosen by compute/storage tier rather than Cosmos-style RUs, and DocumentDB supports multi-document transactions across shards via the transactions API.
